title: The Pocket Garden
story: On Saturday, Sia found an empty shoebox lid. She put it on the courtyard table. "I will make a garden small enough to carry," she told her friend Milo. She cut yellow flowers from paper and folded green paper into grass.
Milo watched her leave one corner empty. "Did you run out of paper?" he asked. "No," said Sia. "That space is for an idea I have not found yet." Then she placed her last flower in the little garden.

Just then, a gust of wind swept across the table. A yellow flower flew into Milo's lap. Two more fell flat. Sia pressed her hands over the box. "My garden will never work outside," she said. Her smile was gone.

Milo picked up a small, smooth stone beside the path. "We cannot stop the wind," he said, "but we can help the flowers stand." They folded a wide paper foot under each flower. Then they put a stone on each foot.

They set the garden on the table again and took their hands away. The next breeze made the paper flowers shake, but they did not fall. Sia let out a long breath. "Your idea gave my flowers strong feet!" she said.

A girl named Ava stood by the blue bench. She had just moved into the building. She watched the two friends but did not come closer. Sia lifted the box. "Would you like to add something?" she asked. Ava stepped toward the table.

"I can make a snail," Ava said softly. She curled a strip of blue paper into a shell. Soon a tiny paper snail sat in the empty corner. "It needs a place to rest," she said. Milo bent a paper leaf over it.

Now the little garden held flowers, stones, and a snail under a leaf. It held three ideas, too. Sia carried it to the bench, and her new friend walked beside her. The box was small, but Sia was glad she had left room for something new.

options: A flowerpot filled with soil
An empty shoebox lid
A basket full of leaves
A large glass jar

She is saving it for a real plant.
She has no paper left for that corner.

multiple_choice.ko: 종이가 부족해서가 아니라, 아직 떠올리지 못한 아이디어를 위한 공간입니다.

Ava makes a small paper snail.

multiple_choice.why: One flower flies away and two fall flat before Sia covers the box.
multiple_choice.ko: 바람에 꽃이 날아가거나 쓰러진 뒤 손으로 상자를 덮습니다.

A bright patch of sunlight

multiple_choice.q: Which detail best shows that Ava wants to join in?
options: She steps closer and offers to make a snail.
She stands by a bench before Sia speaks.

written.q: Was the empty corner a good idea? Tell what you think and use a detail from the story. Write 2-3 complete sentences.
written.sample: Yes, I think the empty corner was a good idea. Ava used it for her paper snail. Leaving space helped Sia include a new friend.
written.ko: 자기 의견과 본문의 구체적인 근거가 서로 연결되는지 봅니다.
written.must: 명확한 의견 + 본문 사실 1개 이상 + 그 사실이 의견을 뒷받침하는 설명
written.accept: 다른 의견도 가능합니다. 예: "Sia could fill the corner first and move a flower later. Paper flowers can be moved, as we see when the wind blows them over." 사실과 논리가 맞으면 인정합니다.

drawing.task: Add one new thing to the tiny paper garden. Draw it, label at least two parts, and write two sentences explaining what it is and how it helps.

title: The Moon in the Puddle
story: The rain stopped just before bedtime. Sia put on her yellow boots and walked into the garden with Grandpa. A round moon shone above the gate. Then Sia looked down. Another moon was shining in a puddle beside her feet.
"There are two moons!" she said. She took a quick step closer. Her boot splashed the edge of the puddle, and the little moon broke into silver strips. Sia stood still. "Oh no. Did I break the moon?"

Grandpa did not answer at once. "Look up," he said. Sia lifted her head. The moon above the gate was still round. Nothing was missing from it. She looked down again, then up. "That one has not changed," she said.

They crouched beside the puddle. This time, Sia gently touched the water with one finger. Small ripples spread across it. The silver shape shook and stretched. "The water is moving the picture," she said. "Can we make it round again?"

"Let us wait and see," Grandpa said. They kept their hands and boots still. Slowly, the ripples faded. The bright circle appeared again. Grandpa explained that the puddle showed a reflection: a picture of something on its shiny surface.
A lamp beside the gate made a yellow line in the water. Sia moved to the other side of the puddle. From there, she could no longer see the moon in it. But the real moon was still above her.

Back inside, Sia drew two pictures in her notebook. In the first, the water was still and the reflection was round. In the second, ripples made it wavy. Under both pictures, she drew the same round moon in the sky.

"Now I know which thing changed," she told Grandpa. Then she looked out of the window. A star had appeared beside the moon. Sia opened her notebook to a fresh page. "Tomorrow, can we look for a star in the puddle, too?"

options: In her notebook
Inside a yellow lamp
In a puddle by her feet
On the garden gate
multiple_choice.ko: Sia가 발 옆 웅덩이에 비친 달을 봅니다.

multiple_choice.ko: 다가가다가 장화로 웅덩이 가장자리를 튀긴 것이 첫 변화의 원인입니다.

title: The Silent Dragon
art_style: 굵은 잉크 선과 선명한 과슈 색면
story: Sia and Leo made a dragon puppet from an old cereal box. They painted it green and gave it a long tail. On Friday evening, they planned a show for Sia's parents. Leo had been practicing a huge dragon roar.

Just before the show, Mom came into the room. "The baby is asleep," she said. "Please keep your show quiet." Leo lowered his puppet. "A dragon without a roar?" he asked. "How will anyone know what it is doing?"

Sia held up a tiny mouse puppet. She moved it toward the dragon. Then she made the dragon jump backward and hide its face behind its tail. Leo smiled. "That great big dragon is afraid of a little mouse!" he said.

"You understood, and I did not say anything," Sia said. They hung a white sheet between two chairs. Dad placed a lamp behind it. The puppets made dark shadows on the sheet. Now even the tiny mouse was easy to see.

At first, Leo moved the dragon too quickly. Its shadow darted from side to side. Sia could not follow the action. They tried again with three slow movements: a sleepy nod, a sudden jump, and a long, careful look at the mouse.

Mom and Dad sat in the front row. The dragon nodded off. The mouse crept closer. Suddenly, the dragon jumped and hid behind its tail. Then the mouse offered it a paper flower. The dragon slowly came out and bowed.

Mom covered her mouth as she laughed. Dad lifted both hands and waved them instead of clapping. Behind the closed bedroom door, the baby kept sleeping. Leo looked at the quiet audience. Their smiles told him that the story had worked.

After the show, Sia asked whether Leo missed his roar. He shook his head and made the dragon give one tiny wave. "I thought a big dragon needed a big noise," he whispered. "But this one had plenty to say without it."

options: An old cereal box
A green wool blanket
A large paper plate

multiple_choice.ko: 오래된 시리얼 상자를 재료로 용 인형을 만듭니다.

multiple_choice.ko: 뒤로 뛰고 꼬리로 얼굴을 숨기는 동작으로 두려움을 표현합니다.

multiple_choice.q: In paragraph 5, what does "darted" mean?

Fell slowly to the floor
multiple_choice.ko: 너무 빨리 좌우로 움직여 동작을 따라가기 어렵다는 문맥입니다.

multiple_choice.q: Why do the children use slower movements?

multiple_choice.ko: 빠른 움직임은 이해하기 어려워, 느린 동작으로 이야기를 분명하게 전달합니다.

multiple_choice.ko: 생쥐가 종이꽃을 건넨 뒤 용이 천천히 나와 인사합니다.

multiple_choice.q: How does Leo know the quiet show has worked?
options: The baby opens the bedroom door.
The lamp makes a louder sound.

The dragon gets a new paper tail.
multiple_choice.ko: 조용한 관객들의 미소를 보고 이야기가 전달됐음을 알아차립니다.

multiple_choice.q: Which message fits the story best?

multiple_choice.ko: 동작과 표정에 해당하는 인형의 움직임으로 말 없이도 이야기를 전합니다.

written.q: Why do the slower puppet movements help the audience? Write 1-2 complete sentences.
written.sample: The slower movements make each action clear. The audience has time to see what the dragon is doing.

written.sample: Dad lifts his hands and waves them instead of clapping. This shows he likes the show without waking the baby.
written.ko: 박수 대신 한 행동과 그 이유를 설명합니다.

written.sample: No, he changes his mind. The audience understands the quiet show and smiles. Leo says the dragon had plenty to say without a big noise.
written.ko: Leo의 처음 생각과 마지막 생각의 변화를 확인합니다.
written.must: 생각이 바뀜 + 관객 반응 또는 마지막 말의 근거

title: The Longer Way
story: Ben brought an old park map on their picnic walk. Sia carried apples, and Aunt May carried the sandwiches. Their picnic spot was an oak tree across the stream. Ben traced a short path with his finger. "The wooden bridge is quickest," he said.

But a wooden barrier blocked the bridge. One board was missing from the middle. Aunt May stopped with the children well before the barrier. Ben stared at his map. "There is no barrier here," he said, tapping the little bridge symbol.
"The map shows how the park looked when it was printed," Aunt May said. "The park can change." Ben folded his arms. He had wanted to lead the way. Now his neat plan seemed to end at a broken bridge.

Sia noticed a small hut near the path. A park worker stood outside. "Could we ask about another way?" she said. They walked over together. The worker pointed to a path beside the stream. It led to a stone bridge farther away.

Aunt May checked the route with the worker before they set off. Ben worried that the walk would take longer. "It will," she said, "but it is open and safe." Sia put the map beside his hand. "You can still guide us."

Along the new path, they found tiny purple flowers. A duck slipped into the stream, leaving a wide trail in the water. Ben began marking these places on the map. Soon he was looking up at the park more often than down at the paper.

They crossed the stone bridge and reached the oak tree. At the picnic table, Sia drew their new route. Ben added a cross over the closed wooden bridge. "We should write today's date," he said. "It might be fixed next time."

The sandwiches tasted just as good after the longer walk. Ben spread the map beside his plate. His new line bent around the stream instead of going straight across. "My first plan was shorter," he said, "but it missed some of the best parts."

multiple_choice.q: Where do the three walkers plan to have their picnic?
options: At the small park hut
Beside the wooden barrier
Under an oak tree across the stream
In the middle of the stone bridge
multiple_choice.ko: 목적지는 시내 건너편의 참나무입니다.

multiple_choice.q: Why can they not use the wooden bridge?
options: The old map has been lost.
It is blocked and has a missing board.
The path beside it is too long.

multiple_choice.ko: 차단물이 있고 다리 가운데 판자 하나가 빠져 있어 이용할 수 없습니다.

multiple_choice.q: Who suggests asking about another way?
options: Ben
Aunt May
The park worker
Sia
multiple_choice.ko: Sia가 안내소 근처 직원을 보고 다른 길을 물어보자고 제안합니다.

multiple_choice.q: In paragraph 5, what does "route" mean?
options: A way to get from one place to another
A picture of a duck in the water
A kind of food for a picnic
A tool for fixing wooden boards
multiple_choice.ko: 직원에게 확인하고 출발하는 목적지까지의 길을 뜻합니다.

multiple_choice.q: What does Aunt May do before they take the new path?
options: She asks Ben to throw away the map.
She carries everyone over the stream.
She checks the way with the park worker.
She moves the wooden barrier aside.
multiple_choice.ko: 새 길을 가기 전에 직원과 경로를 확인합니다.

multiple_choice.q: Why does Ben want to put the date on the map?
options: The bridge might be repaired later.
The sandwiches might need more time.
The stream might disappear at once.
The oak tree might change its name.
multiple_choice.ko: 다음 방문 때 다리가 고쳐져 있을 수 있으므로 언제 확인한 정보인지 남기려 합니다.

multiple_choice.q: Which detail shows Ben becomes interested in the new path?
options: He folds his arms near the barrier.
He first chooses the shortest path.
He worries about a longer walk.
He marks the flowers and duck on the map.
multiple_choice.ko: 불만을 보이던 처음과 달리 발견한 꽃과 오리를 지도에 기록합니다.

multiple_choice.q: Which message fits the whole story best?
options: The shortest route is always the best.
A changed plan can lead to good discoveries.
An old map should never be used again.
A good leader never asks for help.
multiple_choice.ko: 우회하면서 새 풍경을 발견하고 지도를 보완하므로 계획 변경의 좋은 면을 보여 줍니다.

written.q: Why is the map different from the park at the bridge? Write 1-2 complete sentences.
written.sample: The map shows the park when it was printed. The wooden bridge has changed since then, so the old map does not show the barrier.
written.ko: 지도에 담긴 시점과 현재 상태를 구분합니다.
written.must: 지도는 과거 모습 + 현재 다리는 막혀 있음
written.accept: "The map is old and has not been updated."도 현재의 변화를 설명하면 인정합니다.

written.q: How does Sia help Ben keep taking part after his first plan fails? Write 1-2 complete sentences.
written.sample: Sia puts the map beside Ben's hand and tells him he can still guide them. She gives him a way to help with the new plan.
written.must: 지도를 건네거나 계속 안내할 수 있다고 말함 + 새 계획에도 참여하도록 도움
written.accept: 직원에게 다른 길을 물어보자고 한 행동도 Ben이 계속 안내할 길을 찾게 했다는 설명과 연결하면 인정합니다.

written.q: Was the longer walk worth taking? Give your opinion and a story detail. Write 2-3 complete sentences.
written.sample: Yes, it was worth taking. They used a safe bridge and saw flowers and a duck. Ben found interesting places he would have missed on the short path.
written.ko: 선택에 대한 의견을 본문 근거로 설명합니다.
written.must: 의견 + 안전·발견·소요 시간 중 본문 근거 + 이유
written.accept: 아쉬웠다는 의견도 인정합니다. 예: 더 오래 걸려 피곤할 것 같지만 열린 안전한 길을 택해야 했다고 설명할 수 있습니다. 차단된 다리를 건너는 해결책은 본문 조건과 맞지 않습니다.

drawing.title: Draw another good route
drawing.task: Invent a park map with a closed path and a different safe route to a picnic spot. Label at least two places.
drawing.hint: Add one surprising thing to discover along your new route.
drawing.writing_task: Write 2 sentences: Which way will you go, and what will you discover?
drawing.model_ko: 예시 그림: 막힌 산책로에는 X를 표시하고, 작은 연못을 돌아 피크닉 나무로 이어지는 길을 그립니다. "pond"와 "picnic tree"를 표시하고 길 옆에 나비를 그립니다.
drawing.sample: I will take the open path around the pond to the picnic tree. On the way, I will discover butterflies near the flowers.
drawing.alternatives: 공사 중인 길 대신 조각상 정원을 지나는 길, 닫힌 문 대신 다른 입구를 이용하는 길도 가능합니다. 막힌 곳을 통과하지 않고 목적지에 이어지는지 확인합니다.
checks: 두 장소의 이름과 새로운 발견을 표시했나요?
두 설명 문장이 지도의 경로와 맞나요?
drawing.questions: "여기가 막히면 어느 쪽으로 갈까?"  "새 길에서 무엇을 발견하게 될까?"
